summary: Project Evolyte is a 7-slide story that introduces school-age space fans to the machines NASA has left on the Moon, on Mars and in deep space. It follows nine stops in the order they happened: Surveyor 3, the Apollo laser mirrors, the Moon buggies, Viking 1, Sojourner, Spirit and Opportunity, Ingenuity, Pioneer 10 and the Voyagers. Each stop has a short story, a fun fact and a chip showing whether the machine is quiet or still working. A "They kept going" slide compares what engineers planned with what happened, such as Ingenuity's 5 planned flights versus 72. The story answers the challenge by treating retired hardware as characters, so young readers learn the science each machine made possible. It matters because every mission builds on the ones before it.
details: What it does: a short, visual story that takes students from the Moon to Mars to deep space, one machine at a time. Benefits and impact: it gives young learners a friendly first look at real space hardware and the science behind it. Tools: Claude Slides, with Fredoka and Nunito Sans fonts and a small illustration drawn in the slide's own graphics; no NASA logos or images. What is creative: the machines are told as characters in the order they happened, with a status chip for each. What we considered: short sentences for young readers, readable contrast, one idea per slide, and fitting the 7-slide limit.
